disclaimer: Eligibility, age limits, medical standards and intake processes in sports, maritime and aviation are set by regulators and can change every cycle. Treat this page as a starting map and confirm details with DG Shipping, DGCA, the Sports Authority of India and each institute.

items.title: Sports Management
items.summary: The business side of sport: events, leagues, marketing, athlete representation and facility management.
items.after: After Class 12 (BBA / BA in sports management) or after graduation (MBA / PG diploma in sports management)
route: Choose a recognised BBA, BA or PG programme in sports management.
Intern with leagues, clubs, federations or event agencies.
Build skills in marketing, finance, data and communication.
items.bodies: Universities and institutes including the National Sports University, Imphal; private sports-business schools

items.title: Sports Medicine & Sports Science
items.summary: Medical care, injury prevention, rehabilitation, nutrition and performance analysis for athletes.
items.after: After Class 12 (PCB) for MBBS, BPT or nutrition degrees; then specialise
route: MBBS (via NEET-UG) followed by a postgraduate programme or diploma in sports medicine, where available.
BPT / MPT with a sports-physiotherapy specialisation.
B.Sc / M.Sc in sports science, nutrition or exercise physiology.
items.bodies: Medical colleges, SAI centres, National Sports University, sports-science departments

items.title: SAI Academies & Khelo India
items.summary: Government-run training pathways for young athletes with stipend, coaching and sports science support.
items.after: As early as school age, selection by trials or talent identification
route: Perform well at district, state and national competitions.
Apply through trials and announcements by the Sports Authority of India (SAI) and Khelo India.
Join a SAI Training Centre, Academy or Centre of Excellence for your sport.
items.bodies: Sports Authority of India (SAI); Khelo India programme of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports

items.title: NIS Coaching Certification
items.summary: The National Institute of Sports (NIS), Patiala, trains and certifies coaches; its diploma is a recognised coaching qualification in India.
items.after: After Class 12 or graduation; eligibility and sport-specific criteria vary, and past athletes often get preference
route: Check NIS Patiala's current admissions notice for eligible sports and age.
Complete the diploma or advanced coaching programme.
Work as a coach in academies, schools, state associations and SAI centres.

items.title: Sports Quota Government Jobs
items.summary: Many central and state departments recruit outstanding athletes directly or through reserved sports-quota posts.
items.after: Depends on the post; typically Class 10, Class 12 or graduation plus medal-level performance
route: Win at recognised national or international events as listed in the recruitment notification.
Apply to railways, banks, police and public-sector sports quotas as notified.
Keep certificates and event documents verified.
items.bodies: Railways, public sector undertakings, state police and sports departments

items.title: Merchant Navy (IMU-CET)
items.summary: Officers on cargo and passenger ships, either on the deck side (navigation) or the engine side (marine engineering).
items.after: After Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics for degree programmes; other entry routes exist for Class 10 / diploma holders
route: Appear for IMU-CET for B.Tech (Marine Engineering), B.Sc (Nautical Science) and related programmes at the Indian Maritime University and affiliated institutes.
Clear the DG Shipping medical fitness standards (including vision for deck roles).
Complete pre-sea training and onboard cadet training; then sit competency exams for higher ranks.
items.bodies: Indian Maritime University (IMU); Directorate General of Shipping (DG Shipping) approves institutes and courses

items.title: Commercial Pilot (DGCA CPL)
items.summary: Fly airlines, cargo and charter aircraft after earning a Commercial Pilot Licence from the Directorate General of Civil Aviation.
items.after: After Class 12 with Physics and Mathematics (can be through NIOS) and minimum age as per DGCA
route: Get a DGCA Class 1 and Class 2 medical certificate.
Train at a DGCA-approved flying school or Flying Training Organisation, including IGRUA (Rae Bareli).
Pass the DGCA ground exams and the radio-telephony licence, then complete the required flying hours for the CPL.
Apply for first-officer roles and, with experience, command roles.
items.bodies: Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA); approved Flying Training Organisations

items.title: Aircraft Maintenance & Cabin Crew
items.summary: Non-pilot aviation careers: Aircraft Maintenance Engineer (AME), airport operations and cabin crew roles.
items.after: After Class 12 (PCM) for AME; Class 12 or graduation for cabin and ground roles
route: AME: choose a DGCA-approved CAR-147 institute for the licence course.
Cabin crew: complete airline selection and safety training.
Airport and ground roles: look at hospitality, logistics and aviation-management programmes.
items.bodies: DGCA-approved institutes; airlines and airport operators

items.title: Fine Arts (BFA)
items.summary: Painting, sculpture, applied art and printmaking, leading to careers as artists, illustrators, curators and art teachers.
route: Apply to BFA programmes through university or institute entrance and portfolio rounds.
Build a portfolio and exhibit work.
Move into studios, galleries, teaching, illustration or design.

items.title: Design (NIFT / NID / UCEED)
items.summary: Fashion, product, communication and industrial design through India's best-known design institutes.
items.after: After Class 12 in any stream (some exams have stream-specific rules)
route: NIFT: entrance with a General Ability Test and a Creative Ability Test, then a situation test where applicable.
NID: Design Aptitude Test (DAT) in prelims and mains stages.
UCEED: for B.Des at IIT Bombay, IIT Delhi and other participating institutes.
items.bodies: NIFT, NID, IITs and private design universities

items.title: Film, Animation & VFX
items.summary: Direction, cinematography, editing, sound, animation and visual effects for film, streaming, advertising and games.
items.after: After Class 12 in any stream (diploma or degree programmes); film institutes also offer postgraduate courses
route: Choose between degree, diploma and film-institute programmes.
Build a showreel and short films while studying.
Work in studios, production houses and freelancing to grow experience.
items.bodies: Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), Satyajit Ray Film & Television Institute (SRFTI), design and animation institutes

items.title: Performing Arts
items.summary: Music, dance, theatre and acting careers, with training in universities, gurukuls and drama schools.
items.after: After Class 10 or 12, with audition or entrance rounds in many institutes
route: Choose a formal degree or a guru-led course.
Perform regularly and build a body of work.
Work in performance, teaching, production or media.
items.bodies: Universities, drama schools, music and dance academies
